sections.description: This section introduces the causative pathogen, its biological characteristics, and the clinical spectrum of infection it produces in humans, establishing the baseline for the patient's initial presentation.
subtopics: Microbiology and habitat of C. canimorsus
Routes of human transmission (bites, scratches, and close contact)
Clinical manifestations: From isolated meningitis to fulminant sepsis
Pathophysiology of C. canimorsus-induced sepsis and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
Challenges in laboratory diagnosis: Fastidious growth and the role of molecular sequencing

sections.section_title: Clinical Evolution: Distinguishing Sepsis-Related DIC from TMA
sections.description: This section focuses on the clinical reasoning required to differentiate early sepsis-induced complications from the later development of a thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA).
subtopics: Initial presentation: Septic shock, pancytopenia, and acute kidney injury (AKI)
Recognizing DIC in the context of bacterial bacteremia
The clinical 'pivot': Identifying isolated hemolysis and persistent thrombocytopenia during clinical improvement
Laboratory indicators of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA): Schistocytes, LDH, and haptoglobin
The challenge of 'hidden' CM-HUS: How severe sepsis can mask early TMA symptoms

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Workup and Differential Diagnosis of TMA
sections.description: This section details the systematic process of ruling out other forms of TMA and confirming the diagnosis through laboratory, imaging, and pathological findings.
subtopics: Defining Thrombotic Microangiopathy (TMA)
Differential diagnosis: Ruling out Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) via ADAMTS13 activity
Ruling out Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC-HUS) via PCR
Interpreting the Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT) and its potential false positives
Renal biopsy findings: Identifying ischemic glomeruli and fibrin thrombi
Complement testing: Limitations of standard C3/C4 levels in diagnosing CM-HUS

sections.description: This section explains the underlying biological mechanisms of CM-HUS, focusing on complement dysregulation and the concept of infectious triggers.
subtopics: Mechanism of the alternative complement pathway
Genetic predispositions: Variants in factors H, I, B, and CD46
The 'Second Hit' theory: How infections (like C. canimorsus) trigger disease in susceptible hosts
The clinical paradox: Complement as a defense mechanism vs. a driver of endothelial damage
Infection-triggered CM-HUS vs. hereditary complement deficiencies

sections.description: This section covers the management of CM-HUS, emphasizing the transition from supportive care to targeted complement blockade and the unique challenges posed by active infection.
subtopics: Role of Plasma Exchange (PEX) as a bridging therapy
Eculizumab: Mechanism of action and the importance of early initiation for renal outcomes
The clinical dilemma: Managing risk of encapsulated bacterial infection during complement blockade
Prophylactic measures: Vaccination and antimicrobial coverage during eculizumab therapy
Prognostic factors: Impact of time-to-treatment on renal recovery and haematological remission
